key_insight: ROWBench highlights that current video/world models are still weak at faithfully rendering fine-grained events exactly as specified by a program. It introduces PROWBench to test whether models can visually follow explicit rules, not just produce realistic-looking videos.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of benchmarks for evaluating whether programmable world models obey detailed, program-specified dynamics and interactions. Existing evaluations focus more on visual quality or broad controllability than exact event fidelity.
method: Introduces PROWBench, a benchmark of 170 programmatically constructed episodes designed to probe rule-following in generated video.
Evaluates whether video models render specific world events and interactions as specified by executable programs.
Targets fine-grained adherence rather than only realism, instruction following, or general physical plausibility.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more rigorous way to measure whether world models can serve as reliable components for game engines and interactive simulation. It helps identify models that look plausible but fail to execute exact specified behavior.

paper_title: ROWBench: Do Video Models Render What the Program Specifies?
